title: Onprem CP transition checklist: TF compatibility & rotation plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an operations-first transition checklist and notes bundle for migrating a new on-prem/private control plane (CP) installation from 'sandbox' Terraform modules to our production-compatible TF module set, with explicit scaling, instance rotation, and upgrade/rollback scenarios. This is intended as a field guide for SRE/Platform engineers who own cutover and early lifecycle ops for customer-managed control planes.

Scope:
- Initial setup from infra network to CP services (control-plane API, datastore, operator agents)
- Terraform module compatibility notes (v0.9 -> v1.2 migration patterns)
- Scaling events and horizontal/vertical resizing checklist
- Operator rotation and KMS/secret rotation plan
- Upgrade window runbook and rollback decision trees
- Minimal smoke tests and monitoring/alert recipes to validate health post-change

Fast contacts (on-call rotation):
- Primary: Asha Patel (owner) — asha@redwood.ai — Slack: @ashap
- Secondary: Diego Morales — diego@redwood.ai — Slack: @diegom
- Pager & escalation: eng-sre-oncall (pager duty)
- Slack channel: #private-cp-ops

Pre-cutover checklist (must be green before TF apply):
- Network & DNS
  - Confirm VPC subnets and routing exist and match module expectations (public/private subnets).
  - Verify /etc/hosts and internal DNS entries will be created by the post-provisioning job or by API.
  - Confirm CIDR allocations do not overlap customer onprem ranges.
- Secrets & KMS
  - Ensure KMS key policy permits CP service account + Redwood support service account.
  - Validate secret retrieval with a smoke script: 
    - curl -sS --header "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" https://kms.example.local/v1/secrets/test
  - Have rotation keys staged (old/new) and document key IDs.
- Terraform state & backend
  - Backend must be remote (S3/GCS/OSS-compatible) with locking enabled.
  - Create an explicit state-lock test before real changes: terraform init + terraform plan (no-op)
  - Snapshot current state: terraform state pull > state-before-YYYYMMDD.json
- Operator & images
  - Confirm container registry credentials (read-only) exist and image digests are pinned, not floating tags.
  - List of required images and digests committed to repo: private-cp/images-lock.txt
- Backups and restore tests
  - Full etcd snapshot and test restore in staging.
  - Verify DB read replicas and point-in-time recovery windows.

Terraform module compatibility notes (v0.9 -> v1.2):
- Major changes summary:
  - module.network: changed variable names (vlan_id -> network_segment_id). Provide mapping in locals when upgrading.
  - module.kms: now expects kms_key_arn and key_rotation_enabled (default true). If you rely on manual rotation, set to false explicitly.
  - module.controlplane: split into controlplane-api and controlplane-operator submodules; resource names changed.
- Migration steps:
  1) Create a compatibility shim: locals.tf that maps legacy var names to new module inputs. Keep for one deploy and plan to remove after successful cutover.
  2) Run terraform plan with -target on network resources first. Confirm no destructive changes to compute.
  3) Use terraform import for existing resources whose resource IDs changed in the new modules (document each import command).
- Example shim snippet (add to legacy TF):
  locals {
    legacy_vlan = var.vlan_id
  }
  module "network" {
    source = "git::ssh://.../tf-modules/network.git?ref=v1.2"
    network_segment_id = local.legacy_vlan
  }

Scaling runbook — horizontal scale (add nodes):
- Trigger: CPU sustained > 65% across API servers for 5m OR queue depth spike for 3m.
- Steps:
  1) Increase replica_count in module.controlplane_api and run terraform apply with plan review.
  2) Validate autoscaler configuration (if present) does not conflict with reserved capacity.
  3) Post-apply tests: 
     - curl -f https://cp.example.local/healthz (expect 200 for all pods)
     - kubectl -n cp get pods -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff (zero expected)
  4) Lower LB drain timeout during scale to speed traffic redistribution (documented args).

Scaling runbook — vertical (larger instance types):
- Trigger: memory pressure, or single-node bottleneck for stateful components (etcd, db).
- Steps:
  1) Plan maintenance window (requires brief downtime for stateful components).
  2) Terraform change: instance_type -> new value; increase disk if recommended.
  3) For etcd: perform safe leader transfer, snapshot, then take node down and replace. Ensure quorum preserved.

Rotation plan (instance & key rotation):
- Rotation goals: replace nodes without service disruption; rotate KMS keys and service account secrets safely.
- Node rotation sequence (safe draining):
  1) Identify target node(s) for rotation.
  2) Cordon and drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force (if necessary).
  3) terraform taint the instance resource or replace via lifecycle replace_when_needed.
  4) Apply and wait for new node to pass readiness and for all pods to be scheduled back.
- KMS/secret rotation sequence (dual key strategy):
  1) Add new key to KMS and mark as secondary.
  2) Update CP config to read both old and new key IDs (backwards-compatible decryption).
  3) Re-encrypt or stage rewrap operations for stored secrets.
  4) After validation, switch primary key and retire the old key after 7 days.

Upgrade window runbook (minor upgrades and patch releases):
- Pre-upgrade:
  - Announce maintenance window to customer contacts and internal slack.
  - Run pre-checks: smoke, backup, state snapshot.
  - Generate canary plan for subset of API nodes.
- Canary upgrade (recommended):
  1) Upgrade 1 API node + operator subset and run acceptance tests for 30 minutes.
  2) If anomalies: roll back canary using terraform apply with saved state snapshot or rollout previous image digest.
- Full upgrade:
  - Proceed in waves: API nodes -> operator -> stateful components (etcd, db).
  - Enforce post-wave verification gates (health endpoints, query latency, error rates).

Rollback decision tree (high level):
- If canary fails (>=1 severe error or >5% error rate increase): rollback canary and stop.
- If full upgrade introduces persistent errors >SLO thresholds for 15 minutes and not auto-healing: initiate immediate rollback plan:
  - Revert TF to previous state snapshot: terraform state push state-before-YYYYMMDD.json (only after confirming plan).
  - If state push impossible, revert by re-pinning images to prior digest and restarting operator.

Smoke tests (post-change sanity checks):
- API Liveness: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://cp.example.local/healthz (expect 200)
- Auth flow: run short token exchange against KMS and ensure token TTLs are sane.
- Storage: run a write/read test to CP datastore (create ephemeral namespace, write key, read back).
- Telemetry: make sure metrics are received on prometheus push gateway and that new instances are scraped.

Monitoring & alerts to tune during change:
- Critical alerts: controlplane_api_down, etcd_quorum_loss, cp_db_unavailable, high_api_error_rate
- Soft alerts to watch: pod_restart_rate, cpu_bursting, queue_depth_spike
- Dashboards: per-route latency; token-level cost delta (for hosted parity checks); operator reconciliation lag

Known gotchas and gotchas mitigation:
- Module variable renames -> causes many terraform diffs. Always use shim locals for the first apply.
- Floating image tags -> can cause unexpected behavior. Enforce digest pinning in CI.
- KMS permission edge cases: service account vs. root account policies can block decrypts; test with a short-lived token that mimics service account.
- State drift: customers often have manual changes outside TF. Keep a drift log and use terraform import where necessary.

Post-mortem & documentation update tasks (after cutover):
- Update module compatibility matrix with specific customer notes.
- Capture any terraform import commands used and add to repo under docs/imports/<customer>-YYYYMMDD.txt.
- If any manual steps were needed, convert them to an idempotent script and add to infra-scripts repo.

Appendix: quick commands
- Preview plan for only controlplane-api:
  terraform plan -target=module.controlplane_api -var-file=prod.tfvars
- Import example:
  terraform import module.network.aws_subnet.subnet[0] subnet-0a1b2c3d
- Snapshot state:
  terraform state pull > state-before-$(date +%F).json

Questions to resolve before finalizing:
- Decide on enforced key rotation cadence for customer-managed KMS (30/90/180 days).
- Confirm whether our onprem agent should manage DNS entries or we rely on customer DNS automation.
- Decide how long to keep backward-compat shim in repo (recommended: 1 release cycle).

Status & next steps:
- Current status: in_review with eng-private-deploy and SRE.
- Next actions: get Diego sign-off on KMS dual-key flow, run a staged import in staging, and schedule first cutover dry-run for 2024-12-12.

End of doc.
